clue.text: Dishevel us, let nothing be out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are disordered, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded instruction: rumple us all, but keep everything in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be out of place' asks for US, LET and O (nothing) to be rearranged; the surface's 'let nothing be out of place' sounds like a demand for neatness.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel hair is to rumple and disarrange it, the same as mussing it up.

clue.text: Eels are wriggling free

indicators.note: something wriggling twists about, so the letters of the two words squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: Eels that wriggle about slip loose from a net or hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a captive is to let it go, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Before delivery less than a dozen were held in a South African province

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, so the number goes within the province's name

parts.note: Natal is a former province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal
ten is a number smaller than twelve

explanation.surface: Something about events in South Africa before a delivery, with fewer than a dozen people involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal was a South African province until 1994; 'held in' signals the container, and 'were' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal care happens before a baby is born, delivery being childbirth.

clue.text: Rascal, one with chips perhaps

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A mischievous rogue who also has a chip on the shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with chips perhaps' defines by a typical serving: breaded prawns with chips are a pub classic; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, commonly served in British pubs alongside chips.

clue.text: Display no end of red meat

indicators.note: with no end, the word red loses its final letter

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A butcher showing off meat that is barely red at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to show it, to bring it into view.

clue.text: Game allowed in the road

indicators.note: the word for allowed goes inside the word for the road

parts.note: a route is a road or way taken
let means allowed, as in 'let them go'

explanation.surface: A game permitted to be played out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'the' only links, and 'Game' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Spiteful woman at home in the earth

definitions.meaning: a female fox lives in an earth, the fox's burrow

explanation.surface: A bitter woman who feels most comfortable underground.
explanation.walkthrough: A fox's den is called an earth, so the creature at home there is a fox, here the female one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a female fox and, figuratively, a quarrelsome shrewish woman.

clue.text: Heavenly body needs a body building drug

parts.note: anabolic steroids are drugs used to build muscle

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder's need for drugs, framed as a heavenly physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' only links; the surface plays 'heavenly body' as a fine physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun is a celestial object.

clue.text: Too particular about seaside resort

parts.note: over can mean about, as in 'argue over something'
Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone being far too fussy about a holiday town on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnice means excessively fastidious or fussy.

clue.text: Don makes citation about nine

indicators.note: one word goes round another, so the citation wraps the number

parts.note: a quote is a quotation or citation
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A university lecturer quoting a source on the number nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, but it is the title of Cervantes' deluded knight; 'about' signals the citation going round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is the title before the name of Cervantes' knight-errant hero.

clue.text: Undressed kid made a legal claim by the point

parts.note: sued means took legal action
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: A naked child brought a lawsuit next to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undressed kid' reads as a naked child, but it is leather from a young goat with the flesh side brushed; 'by the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: This leather is made from kid skin with a napped, unfinished surface.

clue.text: A long time in the larder producing a pompous spectacle

indicators.note: the time phrase goes inside the storeroom word

parts.note: a pantry is a larder or food store
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Ages spent in the larder somehow yields a grand display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container, and 'the' and 'producing' only link; the surface reads 'A' as an article, but it belongs to the time phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate ceremonial display, as in a parade with costumes and banners.

clue.text: One that cannot be returned

parts.note: reads as an unreturnable item, but means a tennis serve the opponent fails to touch

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a serve so good that the receiver cannot hit it back scores outright.

clue.text: City still delighted

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
static means not moving, still

explanation.surface: A town at rest and very pleased with itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, in raptures.

clue.text: Endlessly trifling with unimportant matters

indicators.note: without its end, the word for trifling loses its last letter

parts.note: trivial means trifling or petty

explanation.surface: Endlessly fussing over things that do not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are insignificant details or minor facts.

clue.text: Ringing sound vibrating on a screen

indicators.note: something vibrating is shaken about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ringing noise from something shaking on a display screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, echoing quality of sound, as when a bell's tone lingers.

clue.text: Hurry to use the weighing machine

definitions.meaning: a command to go faster, especially in a car
taken literally, to stand upon the scales

explanation.surface: Rushing to weigh oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning 'accelerate' read literally describes stepping onto bathroom scales.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a driver to press the accelerator; literally it is mounting the scales.

clue.text: Silver, a Turkish commander

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver belonging to a commander in Ottoman Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or chief official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Merry es go awry

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Merry es go awry' is garbled by OCR: 'es go' supplies only E, S, G, O of the eight letters, and no source recovers the printed fodder.

clue.text: Appear almost to understand

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: seem means appear, as in 'they seem happy'

explanation.surface: To give the impression of almost grasping something.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp or comprehend it, as in 'I see'.

clue.text: A fabric woven when one chooses

parts.note: twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Cloth woven to order, as and when the customer likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting at will means acting as one pleases, whenever one wishes.

clue.text: Delia's content with an old priest

indicators.note: the contents of a word are the letters inside it, here within the name with its possessive

explanation.surface: Delia is happy to be with a priest of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means what Delia's holds; Eli is the priest of Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was a biblical high priest and judge of Israel.

clue.text: Tending to wear away the statue I have

parts.note: the statue of Eros at Piccadilly Circus in London is the famous one
I've is the contraction of 'I have'

explanation.surface: A statue of mine that is slowly wearing away in the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the statue' is the London landmark at Piccadilly Circus popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosive describes something that gradually wears down or eats away a surface.

clue.text: Party about to come back for a worker

parts.note: Labour is a British political party

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in the return direction

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A political party wanting someone back to represent working people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns RE into ER; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer does manual work, so is a worker.

clue.text: Discharge account then leave

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Settle the bill and then walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' only links; 'Discharge' means release from a charge in court, not pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that clears a defendant releases them from the charge.

clue.text: Statement about wine

parts.note: re means about, concerning
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A formal statement concerning wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is an account or statement of facts.

clue.text: One way to call back, showing indifference

parts.note: one as the article a
a path is a way

indicators.note: going back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness is summoned to court

explanation.surface: A route for calling back, offered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CITE into ETIC; 'showing' sets up the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apathetic lacks interest or concern.

clue.text: Give free medicine to patients?

definitions.meaning: to give medical care to the sick

explanation.surface: Handing out medicine to patients at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'medicine to patients' is a loose description of the verb meaning to give medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone a meal is one sense; to give medical care to the sick is another.

clue.text: Writer to adopt a different pose

indicators.note: a different arrangement of these letters gives the name

explanation.surface: An author asked to strike another pose for the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to adopt' only links; the writer is the ancient Greek fabulist.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables.

clue.text: Conceal most of the wrapper

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: an envelope is a paper wrapper for a letter

explanation.surface: Hiding most of the packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up and so cover or hide completely.

clue.text: Find out when the record stops

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
something over has finished or stopped

explanation.surface: Learning something at the moment the music ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'when' only link; 'stops' is taken as 'is over'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to learn or ascertain something.

clue.text: Representation of good man on a Tuesday

parts.note: ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A portrait of a virtuous man made one Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure representing a person or creature.
